original_question: If f : {-1,1}^n -> [-1,1] has degree at most k, must there exist a coordinate i in [n] with influence Inf_i[f] >= (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?
target_in_paper: The unnumbered problem entry "Aaronson–Ambainis Conjecture" in the paper’s main list of open problems.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation. It has the correct domain {−1,1}^n, codomain [−1,1], degree bound k, existential quantifier over a coordinate i∈[n], and the target lower bound of the form Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}.
missing_details: Make the universal quantifiers explicit: the question is for every n, every degree parameter k, and every bounded real-valued function f on the Boolean cube with degree at most k.
Specify that "degree" means the real multilinear/Fourier degree of f on {−1,1}^n, i.e. the largest size of a subset S with nonzero Fourier coefficient.
Define variance and influence with respect to the uniform measure on {−1,1}^n.
Unpack the notation (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)} as: there exists a universal constant C>0, independent of n, k, and f, such that Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^C.
If the question is meant to be fully stand-alone, include an explicit formula for Inf_i[f], e.g. Inf_i[f] = sum of squared Fourier coefficients over all S containing i.
State the ambient scalar field implicitly used by the paper’s notation: this is a real-valued function and a real multilinear/Fourier expansion, not a polynomial over a finite field.
Clarify that there are no extra hypotheses such as Boolean-valuedness, homogeneity, or nilpotency; the conjecture is about arbitrary bounded real-valued low-degree functions on the cube.
refined_question: For every n,k∈N and every function f:{−1,1}^n→[−1,1] with Fourier expansion f(x)=sum_{S⊆[n]} fhat(S) χ_S(x) satisfying fhat(S)=0 whenever |S|>k, where Var[f]=sum_{S≠∅} fhat(S)^2 and Inf_i[f]=sum_{S∋i} fhat(S)^2 (equivalently, variance and influences are taken with respect to the uniform measure on {−1,1}^n), must there exist a coordinate i∈[n] and a universal constant C>0 such that Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^C?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Aaronson–Ambainis Conjecture, whose statement on PDF p. 7 matches your wording almost verbatim. This paper is a problem list, not a theorem-proof article with numbered Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 items, so the nearest official formulation is this unnumbered entry. The paper’s front matter explicitly says that notation and definitions are taken from standard analysis-of-Boolean-functions conventions rather than redeclared locally, which is why the main remaining task is to make degree, influence, variance, and quantifiers explicit so the question becomes fully stand-alone. The adjacent remarks also confirm the intended scope: the Boolean-valued special case is already known, and a weaker related lower bound is available, so the sharp open problem in this paper is exactly the bounded real-valued low-degree formulation you drafted.
